answer: Each agent identity registers on a shared mesa only after a two-channel interlock proves possession of a distinct physical root, so a cloned key alone cannot occupy it. Redundant cross-checked attestations from independent registrars, wired like a safety-rated vine, force a sybil to duplicate hardware and pass both channels per identity, multiplying cost linearly with sock-puppet count. A single shared thread of trust anchors the design, yet common-mode failure in one registrar can still certify a batch, a limit requiring channel diversity.
